summary.intent: Fix a CI-only flaky E2E test failure in writable-shares.spec.ts where subfolder navigation after a recipient creates a subdirectory was failing intermittently.
summary.outcome: Two bugs were fixed: (1) the API's addShareKeys endpoint incorrectly blocked write-share recipients from adding 'folder' type keys, preventing subfolder navigation; (2) the E2E test had a race condition where parentDirRow.waitFor resolved immediately before async navigation completed. Changes were committed but the PR was not yet created by end of transcript.

repo: The cipher-box project has serial E2E tests in writable-shares.spec.ts — later tests (8.x) depend on state set up by earlier tests (1.x through 7.x), so individual test execution is not possible.

Web3Auth wallet login requires CI-only env vars (VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID, TEST_LOGIN_SECRET); setting NODE_ENV=test locally breaks Web3Auth initialization even though CI uses NODE_ENV=test for relaxed throttling.
The API enforces rate limiting that triggers 429s in local dev (NODE_ENV=development) but is relaxed in CI (NODE_ENV=test).

The shares.service.ts addShareKeys endpoint had an overly broad restriction: it blocked write-share recipients from adding 'folder' type keys to prevent root folder key overwriting, but root folder keys are stored in the shares table, not share_keys — so all folder entries in share_keys are for subfolders.

The SDK's createSharedSubfolder silently swallows addShareKeys errors via a catch block with only console.warn, causing silent data integrity failures where a folder appears in the UI but is not navigable.

The useSharedNavigation hook's navigateToShare/navigateToSubfolder errors are surfaced in the UI as visible error text (e.g., '// ERROR: Failed to open subfolder: ...'), making screenshots diagnostic.
Package rebuild (pnpm build) is required after branch switching if the api-client package has new endpoints — missing exports cause blank white-screen React failures.
The project uses 1Password SSH agent for commit signing; commits fail when the desktop session is not available.

code.finding: Overly restrictive guard blocked write-share recipients from adding 'folder' keyType to share_keys. This broke subfolder navigation for recipient-created subfolders. The guard was intended to prevent root folder key overwriting, but root keys live in the shares table, not share_keys.
New navigateIntoSubfolder(name) method added that double-clicks and then waits for breadcrumbs to contain the subfolder name, replacing the racy doubleClickFolderItem + parentDirRow.waitFor pattern.

Four instances of doubleClickFolderItem + parentDirRow().waitFor({ state: 'visible' }) replaced with navigateIntoSubfolder(). The old pattern was a race: parentDirRow was already visible at the current depth so the wait resolved immediately before async IPNS resolution + metadata decryption completed.
navigateToSubfolder has a catch block that logs errors to console. Error messages appear in the UI as visible text, useful for screenshot-based debugging during E2E failures.

workflow: Playwright test-results/*/test-failed-N.png screenshots are highly diagnostic — error messages rendered in the UI are readable directly from screenshots, sometimes faster than parsing console logs.
error-context.md in test-results captures the page snapshot of the active page context (not all browser contexts), so multi-user tests may show the wrong user's state in the context file.
When debugging E2E failures, adding temporary error detail to UI error messages (e.g., appending the exception message) and re-running makes screenshot-based diagnosis much faster than log parsing.
NestJS watch mode (ts-node --watch) recompiles automatically on file save, but a full restart may be needed after .env changes.
The MCP Playwright browser tool (mcp__playwright__browser_navigate, browser_console_messages) is available for interactive debugging of the running dev server.

friction: Multiple service restart cycles required (API killed by Playwright webServer timeout, web server returning 404 from stale process) before tests could run.
Branch switch caused a stash/unstash cycle that lost in-progress edits, requiring the changes to be re-applied manually.
pnpm build regeneration pulled in Rust docs linter, making it slow and noisy.
NODE_ENV=test locally breaks Web3Auth, making it impossible to run the full E2E suite locally with the same environment as CI — rate limiting (429) masks the real bug in local dev.
The SDK silently swallowing the 403 from addShareKeys meant the API bug produced no visible error at the call site, only a downstream 'No key available' failure much later.
1Password SSH agent unavailability blocked the commit at end of session, requiring user intervention.
